### Observed differences

- The backbone is unchanged: A27 and A29 still appear in every trace in both windows, and before the change the flow ran directly A27 → A28 → A29, with about 99 in 100 of A27's outgoing transitions going to A28 and about 99 in 100 of A28's going to A29. [DIR004, DIR005, POS004, POS005]
- In the later window, three activities that were observed in none of the earlier traces appear: A20 in about 41 in 100 traces, A25 in about 30, and A19 in about 29, each occurring once per trace where it appears. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- These three behave as mutually exclusive alternatives: any pair of them co-occurs in at most about 1 in 100 later traces, and combining the pair profiles, virtually every later trace contains exactly one of the three (roughly a 30/40/30 split), whereas earlier none of them occurred at all. [REL001, REL002, REL006, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- Routing changed accordingly: in the later window only about 44 in 100 of A27's outgoing transitions go to A28, while about 55 in 100 go to one of the new activities (about 22 to A20, 17 to A25, 15 to A19); A28 now goes directly to A29 in about 55 in 100 transitions and to a new activity in about 43; each new activity in turn leads mainly to A28 or A29 (roughly a 55/45 split). [DIR004, DIR005, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- The new activities sit inside the former A27–A28–A29 segment: the A27→A28 step distance grew from 1 step in about 99 in 100 cases to 2 steps in about 55 in 100, the A28→A29 distance grew from 1 to 2 steps in about 43 in 100, and the A27→A29 distance grew from 2 to 3 steps; positionally, the new activities appear at mid-trace relative position (median about 0.52), between A27 (median about 0.46) and A29 (median about 0.57). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, POS001, POS002, POS003]
- Relationally, each pair of a new activity with A27, A28 or A29 went from never co-occurring to co-occurring in about 30–41 in 100 later traces; the new activity always executes after A27 (e.g., A27 before A20 in 40 in 100) and before A29 (A20 before A29 in 39 in 100), with mixed order around A28 (e.g., A20 before A28 in 23 in 100, A28 before A20 in 17). [REL003, REL004, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL005]
- A10's trace participation rose from about 5 in 100 traces earlier to about 13 in 100 later. [OCC001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a specific hypothesis: in the later window, a new mid-process step is inserted into the segment between A27 and A29, executed as one of three nearly mutually exclusive alternatives — A20, A25 or A19 — where previously the flow ran directly A27 → A28 → A29. The new step is reached from A27 in about half of its transitions and leads on to A28 and/or A29, so that essentially every later trace contains exactly one of the three alternatives in place of (or alongside) the former direct hops. This is shown directly and consistently by the rerouted outgoing transitions of A27 and A28, the new co-occurrence and ordering relations (after A27, before A29, mixed around A28), the widened step distances, and the mid-trace positions of the new activities; with 29 qualifying items against roughly 0.54 expected for an unchanged process, the ensemble as a whole is not what random re-splits produce. Limitations: the earlier window only shows that A19, A20 and A25 were not observed, so a genuinely added step cannot be distinguished from previously existing paths that were simply not taken before; and the insertion point is not uniform — the new activity sits between A27 and A28 in about 55 in 100 cases and between A28 and A29 in about 43. [DIR004, DIR005, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL001, REL003, REL007, REL009, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, POS001, POS002, POS003]

Other differences: A10's participation increased from about 5 to about 13 in 100 traces; this increase is not part of the insertion hypothesis above. [OCC001]
